newsitem.title: IRAQ: Jordanian businessmen in Baghdad to strike trade deals.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian businessmen in Baghdad to strike trade deals.

text.p: Thirty-seven Jordanian businessmen are visiting Baghdad to try to win trade contracts with Iraq under an oil-for-food deal signed with the United Nations.
"These businessmen represent all industries in Jordan such as cooking oil, soap and detergents, table salt and others," chairman of Amman Chamber of Industry, Khaldun Abuhassan, told Reuters.

Iraq started limited oil sales on December 10 under a deal signed with the United Nations to buy food and medicine for the Iraqi population affected by U.N. sanctions for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Abuhassan said Jordan had won several contracts to supply Iraq with cooking oil, detergents and table salt under the oil deal.
Iraq has been dependent on Jordan for most of its food supplies in return for supplying Amman with crude oil and by-products which are exempted from the U.N. sanctions.
Two Jordanian ministers were in Baghdad last week to buy Iraqi crude and by-products for 1997.
